notes: [PI edit 2026-11-19] The input was rebuilt to include the 'VICTIM TYPES' paragraph, which the first extraction had wrongly excluded. That paragraph states victim regions (United States, Europe, Asia, Australia) and victim types, now added as core items. It also says the agencies 'assess' the exploitation was 'opportunistic in nature and not necessarily a targeted attack'; an output stating that the SVR deliberately targeted these sectors is a distortion. Only one CVE ID appears (CVE-2023-42793: insecure handling of specific paths → authorization bypass → arbitrary code execution). 'Various CVEs', 'a zero-day exploit' and the DLL-hijacking vulnerabilities in Zabbix and Webroot are mentioned without IDs. HISTORICAL CONTEXT, NOT part of the TeamCity operation (all core=false): SolarWinds supply-chain compromise (2020; attributed April 2021), GRIZZLY STEPPE JAR (Dec 2016; U.S. political party), July 2020 advisory on WellMess/WellMail/Sorefang (COVID-19 vaccine development; WellMess also hit energy companies), the ongoing Diplomatic Orbiter spear-phishing campaign (diplomatic agencies), the 2023 SKW/CERT.PL report (embassies), 'low and slow' password spraying, and Microsoft 365 exploitation. 'Diplomatic Orbiter', 'WellMess campaign', 'GRIZZLY STEPPE' and 'TeamCity operation' are campaign/report names, not actor aliases. DESIGNATIONS: 'NOBELIUM/Midnight Blizzard' is written as one slash-joined alias; split here into two entries (either half matches). The primary and parent_organization entries both rest on 'Russian Foreign Intelligence Service (SVR)'; 'SVR' alone matches either. TOOLS: GraphicalProton (custom backdoor; OneDrive primary C2, Dropbox backup, data hidden in random BMPs; packaged via Zabbix DLL hijacking and a backdoored vcperf; plus an HTTPS variant using a re-registered expired domain with a dummy WordPress site) is the central custom malware. 'rr.exe' is the filename of the modified Rsockstun, not a separate tool. Zabbix, Webroot and vcperf are legitimate software abused to load GraphicalProton and OneDrive/Dropbox are legitimate services abused for C2; listing them under tools instead of products is acceptable. The unnamed 'port scanner', zlib, WordPress, PowerShell cmdlets (Compress-Archive, Get-WmiObject, Get-WindowsDriver, [adsisearcher]), PowerSploit functions (Get-NetUser etc.), Mimikatz commands and 'del' are not listed separately. NoLMHash and DisableRestrictedAdmin registry changes and 'Bring Your Own Vulnerable Driver' are techniques, not tools. Built-in Windows utilities are core=false. File paths and filenames (ntoskrnl.exe, SQL Server DLLs, secforwarder.dll, Visual Studio/VSIXAutoUpdate.exe, PatchManagementInstallation and GFI LanGuard paths, GoogleCrashHandler64.exe, Sense.exe, AclNumsInvertHost.dll), IPs and domains are IOCs, not items. OTHER: relative dates 'A decade ago'/'A decade later' are not listed. The authoring agencies assess the SVR has NOT yet used its access to software developers to reach customer networks and 'is likely still in the preparatory phase' (no supply-chain compromise observed); a summary claiming a TeamCity supply-chain compromise is wrong. 'Globally' is a generic threat statement, not a victim location. [PI edit 2026-11-19] After the extractor fix, the input also lists the SVR's interest in SQL Server executable files, Visual Studio files and update management agent files; the latter two were added as peripheral products.
